messages.subject: Variable Importance
parts:
Hi Stan Community,
In predictive modelling often one encounters a large number of candidate predictors. But in order to achieve better predictive ability one would want to discard predictors that contributes very little in predicting a quantity of interest. A plot showing importance of variables helps in determining variables to be dropped from  a model. Have a look at the example in the following link https://topepo.github.io/caret/variable-importance.html. I am using MTCARS dataset in R as an example to try and achieve a plot such as the one below. Am wondering if there is a possibility of extracting ranks of predictors from Stan fit that can be plotted to produce such a plot as one below.


I appreciate your response

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Re: Variable Importance
parts:
Hi,

That's bit open ended question. The link you provided lists 9 model specific and 3 model independent metrics. What kind of model you are interested in? For model independent metric check the average predictive comparison https://www.google.dk/search?q=average+predictive+comparisons. Note also that simply discarding many predictors which each contribute very little can lead to bad performance http://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11222-016-9649-y , and for linear models and Gaussian processes I recommend projection predictive variable selection (see http://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11222-016-9649-y and http://arxiv.org/abs/1510.04813).

Aki

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Variable Importance
parts:
> On Feb 27, 2017, at 8:28 AM, smockin morry <smocki...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Stan Community,
> In predictive modelling often one encounters a large number of candidate predictors. But in order to achieve better predictive ability one would want to discard predictors that contributes very little in predicting a quantity of interest.

The main motivation I've seen for literally discarding predictors
is that they are collinear with other predictors or there's some
computation bound on which predictors you can use (if the data
has billions of predictors, as in subword data over large natural
language corpora, you need to prune those because 20GB predictor
vectors are impractical.

> A plot showing importance of variables helps in determining variables to be dropped from a model. Have a look at the example in the following link https://topepo.github.io/caret/variable-importance.html. I am using MTCARS dataset in R as an example to try and achieve a plot such as the one below. Am wondering if there is a possibility of extracting ranks of predictors from Stan fit that can be plotted to produce such a plot as one below.

I'd suggest avoiding those ad-hoc selection metrics and reading Aki's
papers. You know it's a bad idea when you see that it's an independent
evaluation. You want to at least select variables stepwise, because what
you want is something that selects the "best" subset of variables. It is
intractable done combinatorially, so people tend to do things like
rank reduction on the predictor matrices or impose L1 priors in the model
itself (or penalty function if you're an MLE sitckler). Those convert the
discrete selection problem into something continuous where there's a hope
of solution.

You can see that one-at-a-time is bad by taking two collinear predictors
that are also collinear with the outcome. The relative contribution of
x[2] after x[1] is quite low, even though independently they look very
"important".

- Bob
